projects.name: Veloce Scrap Flow
projects.tagline: Every kilogram, from weighbridge to dispatch.
projects.summary: A yard operating system for a scrap business: a calculator-fast mobile app for the weighbridge and the sorting floor, and a desktop console that gives management live control across yards and warehouses.

challenge.headline: Mixed loads in. Graded material out. No reliable trail in between.
challenge.body: A scrap yard buys mixed material by weight, sorts it into sellable grades and sells it by the truckload. Every step changes the numbers. Without one system, it is hard to know what is in stock, what is waiting to be sorted and what has actually left the yard — and impossible to see it across several yards.

solution.headline: Built for the yard floor. Controlled from one console.
solution.body: Crita built Scrap Flow as a multi-yard platform. Owners and supervisors work in a mobile app designed like a calculator — big keys, live rates, clear steps — while the platform admin manages yards, warehouses, users and analytics from a desktop console. Every action writes to one inventory ledger, updated in real time.

capabilities.title: Inward at the weighbridge
capabilities.body: Vendor, vehicle and multiple weighments on an LED-style keypad, with photo evidence. Each load becomes a traceable lot.

capabilities.title: Sorting that balances
capabilities.body: Mixed lots are split into finished grades and wastage; a run can’t close until every kilogram is accounted for.

capabilities.title: Sell, allocate, dispatch
capabilities.body: A sale reserves stock; supervisors load vehicles against it. The same kilograms can’t be sold twice or over-dispatched.

capabilities.title: Live stock across warehouses
capabilities.body: Stock on hand, sale thresholds and pending work per yard and warehouse, updated as it happens.

capabilities.title: Admin console & analytics
capabilities.body: Yards, warehouses, users and permissions, with analytics for inward, sorting, dispatch and materials.

capabilities.title: Governance built in
capabilities.body: Every privileged action is recorded in an audit log with before-and-after values.

tour.title: Weight entry, calculator-fast
tour.body: Big keys, a live LED display and kg / ton / tonne switching — built for gloved hands at the weighbridge.

tour.title: Segregation that balances
tour.body: Pick a mixed lot and split it into grades and wastage. Vendor, vehicle and lot history stay attached.

tour.body: Warehouses, supervisors, stock and records for each yard — with the admin able to step inside any yard.

projects.name: Tribal Brew Coffee
projects.type: Café POS, back office & ordering app
projects.tagline: One menu for every outlet — from the counter to the customer’s phone.
projects.summary: A point of sale and back office for a multi-outlet coffee chain, with a customer ordering app. Outlet teams bill at the counter, head office runs the menu, offers, outlets and reports from one system, and customers browse the same live menu on their phones.

challenge.headline: Many cafés, one menu, no single system.
challenge.body: Tribal Brew runs cafés across Bengaluru and Mysuru, plus pop-ups at events. Every counter needs fast billing with the right drink options and taxes, every outlet needs the same menu and prices, and customers now expect to order from their phones.

solution.headline: A counter POS, a central back office and a customer app on one catalogue.
solution.body: Crita built a web POS for the counter — categories, search, drink options with their own prices, GST on every bill and order status — on a back office where head office manages items, modifier groups, discounts, outlets, staff roles and reports. The customer app reads the same live menu and outlet list, so what customers see is what the counter sells.

projects.name: Clario
projects.tagline: Understand your business, not just your numbers.
projects.summary: Crita’s own business-intelligence platform. Clario connects to the systems a business already uses — starting with Zoho Books — and turns them into a clear finance command centre, with an assistant that answers in plain words, from the books.

challenge.headline: The numbers exist. The answers don’t.
challenge.body: Growing businesses keep their figures in accounting software, but turning ledgers into decisions takes reports, spreadsheets and an accountant’s time. Generic AI tools can’t be trusted with financial figures — and every new system adds another place to look.

solution.headline: Connect once. See clearly. Ask anything.
solution.body: Clario gives each client a private workspace. They connect Zoho Books securely, and Clario turns the data into a finance command centre — overview, trends, receivables, payables and balance sheet. Ask Clario answers questions in plain words using the same figures as the reports, and shows where each answer comes from.

capabilities.title: Finance overview

capabilities.title: Ask Clario

projects.name: SMC Task Management
projects.tagline: Field audits, planned, run and closed in one system.
projects.summary: A field-audit operations platform for an audit consultancy. Admins plan visits and define each client’s checklist; executives run every visit from their phone; nothing incomplete is lost between visits.

challenge.headline: Weekly audits, dozens of clients, no single view.
challenge.body: SMC’s executives visit client sites every week to verify operations, stock, accounts and reports — and every client needs a different checklist. Tracking was manual: unfinished items relied on memory to reach the next visit, and management had no live view of progress across the team.

solution.headline: One system, from the admin’s calendar to the executive’s phone.
solution.body: Crita built a role-based platform that turns each audit visit into a structured, trackable workflow. Admins schedule visits and configure checklists per client. Executives open the visit on their phone, complete each item or record why it couldn’t be done, and close it only when the rules are met. Unfinished work carries forward — with admin approval — into the next visit.

capabilities.title: Client-specific checklists
capabilities.body: Each client gets its own task and subtask template, applied to every new visit automatically.

capabilities.title: Rules that keep audits complete
capabilities.body: A visit closes only when required work is done. The MD meeting must be answered and every open item needs a reason.

capabilities.title: Carry-forward with approval
capabilities.body: Unfinished items move into the next visit with their history — after an admin reviews and approves them.

capabilities.title: Progress, trail and summary

capabilities.title: Attendance & leave
capabilities.body: Executives punch in and request leave from the app; admins review attendance and approve requests.

projects.name: AI Sales CRM
projects.type: Sales CRM with an AI co-pilot
projects.tagline: Leads, pipeline and follow-ups — with an AI co-pilot that reads every deal.
projects.summary: Crita’s sales CRM: leads, contacts, a drag-and-drop pipeline, notes and follow-ups in one workspace, with Google Gemini summarising leads, drafting emails and rating the health of the pipeline.

challenge.headline: Deals slip between spreadsheets and memory.
challenge.body: Small sales teams track leads in sheets and inboxes. Follow-ups are forgotten, nobody sees the pipeline’s real value, and every email to a prospect starts from a blank page.

solution.headline: A clean CRM, with an assistant inside every lead.
solution.body: Crita built a CRM around the sales day: a dashboard of pipeline value, closed revenue and win rate; leads by stage, priority and source; a pipeline board; contacts, notes and follow-ups. Gemini reads each lead to suggest the next best action, drafts the email in the chosen tone and rates the pipeline as a whole.

projects.name: City Threads
projects.tagline: Every lot, every bin, every dispatch — accounted for.
projects.summary: A warehouse management system for a textile distributor: barcoded stock units, a visual map of every rack and bin, and an order-to-dispatch flow — with a one-handed phone app for the warehouse floor.

challenge.headline: Two warehouses. A fragmented inventory process.
challenge.body: City Threads stores thread stock across racks and bins in two warehouses. With a fragmented, manual process, finding a lot, knowing which space was free and tracing what moved where took time — and depended on the people who remembered.

solution.headline: A barcode on every lot. A map of every bin.
solution.body: Crita built a warehouse system where every physical lot becomes a stock unit with a permanent ID and barcode. Administrators manage the structure, orders and stock from a desktop workspace; executives receive, move, count, pick and dispatch from their phone — scanning instead of searching.

capabilities.title: Floor operations on the phone

capabilities.title: A ledger that reconciles

projects.name: Veloce Trade
projects.tagline: List, buy, dispatch and get paid — every truckload on one app.
projects.summary: A mobile trading app for Veloce’s network of material sellers, vendors and recyclers. Clients list material for pickup with its pricing; vendors raise purchase orders, send truckloads, assign drivers, labour and vehicles, upload documents and record payments — with every shipment tracked step by step.

challenge.headline: Trades run on calls, paperwork and trust.
challenge.body: Buying and moving material between companies involves pricing, taxes, trucks, weighment slips, invoices and part payments. When that lives in phone calls and paper, nobody can see where a load is, which documents are missing or what is still owed.

solution.headline: One app for every step of a trade.
solution.body: Crita built Veloce Trade as a role-based mobile app. Verified companies list material with pricing that includes TDS, TCS and GST; buyers order against listings; and each fulfilment moves through assignment, loading, documents, invoicing, payment and transit — with the people, the vehicle and the proof attached at every step.

projects.tagline: Every claim approved, reimbursed and measured against budget.
projects.summary: A multi-company expense platform: employees log claims, managers approve them for their department, finance reimburses, and administrators see spend by category, department and payment mode against each department’s budget.

challenge.headline: Receipts in inboxes, approvals in chats.
challenge.body: Expense claims usually travel by email and messaging apps. Approvals are hard to trace, reimbursements are tracked in spreadsheets, and nobody can compare a department’s spending with its budget until the month is over.

solution.headline: One flow, from claim to reimbursement.
solution.body: Crita built Expense Log around companies and roles. Claims carry their category, department and payment mode; managers approve or reject within their department; finance records reimbursements; and budgets are set per department and month, so reports compare spend with plan.

projects.name: Lead Discovery CRM
projects.tagline: Visitors answer a few questions. The team gets a qualified lead.
projects.summary: Crita’s own lead engine: discovery questionnaires published on the website turn visitors into structured leads, every response gets a fit score and next-step coaching, and the team manages clients, questionnaires and responses in one CRM.

challenge.headline: An enquiry is a name and a phone number.
challenge.body: A typical contact form says who got in touch, not what they need. Teams repeat the same questions before every first meeting and have no consistent way to judge which enquiries fit what they offer.

solution.headline: Discovery before the first call.
solution.body: Crita built topic-based discovery questionnaires — branding, workflows and AI, business software, inventory, websites, retail and manufacturing — published on the website and sent as private links. Answers land in a CRM as leads with a fit score, the gaps still open and suggested next steps, beside clients, templates and assignments.

projects.name: Support Portal
projects.tagline: Raise it, track it, resolve it — with every step on record.
projects.summary: Crita’s support desk for its clients: a help centre and knowledge base, a simple form to raise tickets with attachments, and an admin queue where each ticket is assigned, reviewed, approved, resolved and closed — with its full history.

challenge.headline: Support requests get lost in email.
challenge.body: When issues arrive by email and phone, nobody clearly owns them, clients can’t see progress, and there is no record of who approved or changed what.

solution.headline: One portal, for clients and the support team.
solution.body: Crita built a portal with two sides. Requesters raise tickets by type and priority, attach files and follow their status. Administrators work one queue — assign, review, approve, resolve and close — reply to the requester or add internal notes, and every status change is recorded.
